verifiedClaims.claim: Why the I-95 and US-17 corridor through Darien and Brunswick is among southeast Georgia's most dangerous, and what to do after a crash.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No GDOT, GOHS or FARS publication ranks Georgia corridors by danger; GDOT's crash-reporting page publishes no corridor ranking. Georgia-level context that is sourced: one-third of Georgia fatal crashes occur in rural areas although only 21% of Georgians live there, and rural counties recorded 113 speeding-related fatal crashes in 2023, the most in a decade (GOHS 2023 Overview).

verifiedClaims.note: Unsourced ranking. Suggested excerpt: 'Why I-95 and US-17 through Darien and Brunswick carry real crash risk — long-haul trucks, two-lane coastal highway, long rural EMS runs — and what to do after a crash.' The excerpt is published as the Article description.

verifiedClaims.claim: The I-95 and US-17 corridor through Darien and Brunswick is one of Southeast Georgia's most dangerous driving environments, with heavy commercial truck traffic, fatigued long-distance travelers, and rural two-lane roads with no median barriers.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Same as excerpt: no primary source ranks the corridor. The two-lane/no-median description is accurate for US-17 north of Yacht Road in Glynn County and through McIntosh County, but GDOT is widening Yacht Road–SR 99 to four lanes with a 24-foot raised median (PI 0016985 Phase I, 82.27% complete; PI 532650- Phase II, 73%; both 'Under Construction', GeoPI Sept 2026).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: GDOT GeoPI P.I. 0016985 and 532650-; GDOT — Crash Data & Reporting
verifiedClaims.note: Replace 'is one of Southeast Georgia's most dangerous driving environments' with 'is a high-risk driving environment'. Keep the three risk factors; optionally 'rural two-lane roads, much of it without median barriers'.

verifiedClaims.claim: Georgia's two-year statute of limitations (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and comparative fault rule (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, less than 50% at fault) apply to crashes in McIntosh and Glynn counties, while federal trucking regulations provide additional grounds for claims against negligent commercial carriers on I-95.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code §§ 9-3-33, 51-12-33 (Justia; verified in facts-4715/4721/4709)
verifiedClaims.note: Two-year limit and the 50% bar (plaintiff recovers only if less than 50% at fault, award reduced by own share) verified; § 51-12-33 bar unchanged by 2025 SB 68. FMCSRs (49 C.F.R. Parts 390–399) are correctly characterized as evidence of negligence, not a separate cause of action.

verifiedClaims.claim: Interstate 95 and U.S. Highway 17 are the most dangerous roads in the Darien-Brunswick area.

verifiedClaims.claim: When a crash on I-95 or US-17 is fatal, Georgia's wrongful death statute (O.C.G.A. § 51-4-1) allows surviving family members to seek compensation for their loss.
